attachments.description: An array of Attachment objects. For google, linked Google Drive files are not included. For Microsoft, linked One Drive files are not included.

bcc.description:
An array of name/email address pairs that the message was BCC'd to. For received messages, this
is nearly always empty.

body.description: The body of the message. This field is the same as the `body` field in your request.

cc.description: An array of name/email address pairs that the message was CC'd to.

from.description: A list of name/email address pairs that the message was sent from. For transactional send, this will always be one pair.

object.description: The object type of the response (in this case, `message`).

reply_to.description: An array of name/email address pairs that should receive replies to the message.

snippet.description:
A short snippet (the first 100 characters, with HTML tags removed) of the message body. This is
useful for displaying a preview of the message.

opens.description: When `true`, shows that message open tracking is enabled.

links.description: When `true`, shows that link clicked tracking is enabled.

label.description: A label describing the message tracking purpose.

to.description: An array of name/email address pairs that the message was sent to.

attachment_transactional_send.description: A file attachment for a transactional email message.

content_type.description:
The [MIME type](https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Basics_of_HTTP/MIME_types/Common_types) of the attachment, used by the email client to determine how to display the attachment. If you don't provide a type, Nylas infers it from the file name.
The value of this field is exactly the same as the email attachment's `Content-Type` header.
The provider might set additional parameters, such as `name` and `charset`.

Nylas returns an empty `content_type` field if an attachment file name contains non-ASCII characters (for example, accented characters like `ü`). This is because Google can't detect its content type.

filename.description: The file name of the attachment.

content_id.description: (Inline attachments only) The alphanumeric `cid` from the `` tag in the message's HTML. For example, you might see something like `` in the message body. Sometimes, the `content_id` value is contained in angle brackets (for example, ``).

content_disposition.description: (Not supported for Microsoft and EWS) The content disposition of the attachment. Usually, this is `inline` or `attachment` followed by the file name (for example, `inline; filename="some-image.jpeg"`).

is_inline.description: If `true`, indicates that the attachment is an inline file.

size.description: The size of the attachment, in bytes.
